description: Creates a Neblla app and returns its appId. With `decisions` (from neblla_validate_requirements) it scaffolds the matching page with example code for each chosen module (sign-in, store, bookings, community, groups, AI box, friends, inbox, dice…) and writes the app config, its neblla.* modules included; without them it creates a blank index.html. The app is published at <slug or id>.neblla.app on creation (neblla_get_app_url returns the link); later edits stay in its draft until neblla_promote publishes them. Layout: index.html references only main.css and client.js, client.js wraps its code in window.onNeblla, and the files under server/ are top-level code with no DOM access; client and server talk only through messages and state (message.send / message.to('server' | 'presenter' | id, data) / message.on, state.set on the server, state.on and state.get on the client). Neblla can be only the backend of a site hosted elsewhere: the page adds <script src="https://neblla.com/connect/app/<appId>"> and its origin is allowed with neblla_update_app({ addDomain }); nothing is uploaded then. Data: save() data is private, a client reads only its own and there is no query across users over it; users publish entries that every client can list, search and rate through features.community (neblla_get_llms({ section: "comunidad" })). room.data starts with a 10 KB limit that can be changed or turned off; a document two people edit fits better in community entries (64 KB by default). Storage: 5 MB per app in Neblla, 100 MB on Pro, or the developer's own database (neblla_byodb), where the data stops counting but each write still crosses Neblla and costs its payload bytes. The per-user save limit is 10 KB by default, can be raised or turned off. State: what decides the game goes through state.set, and positions through message.send, which is free when direct (a TURN relay, when allowed, counts against the quota); the free tier is 3,579,139 units of payload per day, about 3.6 MB. Purchases: what a user bought is theirs (it changes hands only in a trade both users accept, for the products and tables listed in neblla_update_app({ trade })); neblla.shop.on('purchase') fires only on the buyer's devices, and another user's purchase is checked by room.js with neblla.shop.validate(userId, productId) (a client checks only its own; asking about another answers not_allowed). The guide is neblla_get_llms; its `empezar` section covers when Neblla fits an app and the two-device test for a multiplayer one.

acceptDpa.description: The developer accepts Neblla's terms of use and data processing agreement (DPA), together. Asked once, before their first app (and again when its version changes): the call answers error "dpa_required" with the links until they are accepted. Pass true only once the developer has accepted; the terms are accepted by the developer, not by the caller.

decisions.description: The COMPLETE decision set from neblla_validate_requirements (have_enough_context: true → pass its `decisions` verbatim). Scaffolds the matching pattern with the themed UI pieces for each enabled feature AND writes the app config (its neblla.* modules, connections, serverMode, rooms policy, matchmaking mode, AI payer, theme). The recommended way to create any non-blank app.

projectId.description: The project the app goes to (neblla_projects list). Omitted: the account's Explorer, where apps land by default.

template.description: Legacy alternative to `decisions`: scaffold the canonical files of this page (rooms: the one room example, where the server sets the state and the clients paint it and talk through message; lobby-only; solo-save; home), with no feature pieces and no theme, and the modules of that page. Prefer `decisions`. Omit both for a blank app: only auth and db, the rest with neblla_update_app({ features }).
